speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see an abnormality on your left dorsal hand; can you describe when you first noticed this skin condition and if it has changed in appearance since then?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and history of sun exposure, do you notice the lesion on your left dorsal hand is raised, scaly, or has a rough texture? Also, is it painful or does it bleed easily?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. The description of a rough, sandpaper-like, scaly plaque on the dorsal hand of a 65-year-old with a history of sun exposure is classic for this premalignant lesion. Given your lack of pain or tenderness, I do not suspect an infection or malignancy at this stage, but we should monitor it closely.
